questions.question: Describe the methods Robert Koch and his team developed to study germs.
questions.expected_answer: Koch and his team stained bacteria with dyes so the almost see-through germs could be seen clearly under the microscope. They grew bacteria on solid jelly so that each kind formed a separate colony that could be studied on its own, and Julius Petri designed the Petri dish. Koch photographed bacteria through the microscope so others could see them, and set out rules to prove that a particular germ causes a particular disease.

questions.question: Explain how Koch discovered the germ that causes TB and why it was important.
questions.expected_answer: TB was one of the deadliest diseases, and many believed it was inherited. TB germs grow slowly and have a waxy coat, so Koch worked for months to find the right dyes and methods. He stained the germs, saw them as tiny rods in the lungs of people who had died of TB, grew them and showed they caused TB in animals. On the twenty-fourth of March 1882 he announced the discovery, proving TB is infectious, spread from person to person.

questions.question: How is TB spread, prevented and cured in South Africa today?
questions.expected_answer: TB spreads through the air when a sick person coughs, sneezes or talks, especially in crowded, poorly ventilated rooms. It is prevented by the BCG vaccine given to babies at birth, opening windows, covering coughs and early testing. Tests and treatment are free at government clinics, and TB is cured by taking medicine every day for about six months, finishing the course even when feeling better, so that the germs do not become resistant.
